newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end steady, seen gaining.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end steady, seen gaining.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended the week on a relatively steady note on Friday as the market consolidated after Thursday's sharp rise, but dealers said further gains were likely next week.

"The trend at the moment is higher. I'd expect it to trade higher and test 19,520," said a trader with a European house. "But if it can't regain that level, then it's going to turn south and pull back into 18,500 again," he added.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract added 35 points to close at 19,095 on active turnover of 23,111 lots.
Dealers said the property sector remained well supported after Thursday's rally on the underlying cash market.

"I think this level is going to be acceptable for year-end valuations. I'm sure they'd like to see 20,000 but realistically they know people are going to be wary of bidding it up another 1,000 points," said the trader.
He added, however, that the market's recovery could turn very fragile if the Dow underwent a major correction or the yen strengthened much further.
The dollar was quoted at 122.85/95 yen in afternoon Asian trade after falling below 122.50 earlier in the day.
The March MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 323.7 against its opening 322.5 on volume of 744 lots.

In Taipei, share prices closed at a six-year high after the government announced that Taiwan's Gross Domestic Product for the fourth quarter of 1996 was 6.62 percent, above a forecast of 6.58 percent.
